references.text: The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron earlier in the same chapter, and this verse refers back to their complaints.
Moses has just told the people that the Lord has heard their grumbling, and now he commands Aaron to gather the assembly.
Aaron is called to serve as an intermediary between Moses and the people, a role that is later formalized.
A similar command to gather the assembly to stand before the presence of the Lord.
Moses and Aaron are told to separate themselves from the assembly, and the glory of the Lord appears to the people.
Moses and Aaron gather the assembly, a pattern that is repeated throughout the wilderness journey.
The Lord hears the cries and complaints of his people, a recurring theme about God's attentiveness to his people.
The Lord is near to those who call on him; he hears their complaints.
